wlo.text: 85% of women-led organisations surveyed were hit by funding cuts or reductions in 2025.
Half expect to suspend work or close within a year without urgent financial support.
Two-thirds report that safe spaces and services after gender-based violence have closed or been cut back in their communities.

invest.title: Women-led organisations reach the people others cannot
invest.text: The 85 women-led organisations behind UN Women's 2026 gender alert reach nearly 20 million people in need. They run community kitchens, safe spaces and survivor support, and negotiate access where formal systems have collapsed.

invest.title: Women lead a large share of the local response
invest.text: By the end of 2025 the Sudan Humanitarian Fund had supported more than 1,000 mutual aid groups, and over one third of them were women-led. US$25 million went to mutual aid groups in 2025.

invest.title: Small grants open the door
invest.text: Since 2020 the Women's Peace and Humanitarian Fund has supported 110 women's organisations in Sudan. Close to half received UN funding for the first time.

invest.title: Women keep farms running
invest.text: In CARE's 2025 survey of 492 farmers in Darfur and South Kordofan, 87% were women, as men migrated or joined armed groups. Access to finance and inputs is their main barrier. CARE calls for funding women's farming groups directly.

invest.title: Room to grow the economy
invest.text: Women make up about 30% of Sudan's labour force. Recovery that brings more women into paid work, farming value chains and enterprise adds income for whole households.

invest.title: Missing from the peace table
invest.text: Women mediate local conflicts and negotiate humanitarian access, yet they have had no meaningful role as negotiators in the official peace talks of the past three years.

points.text: 12.4 million people need services after gender-based violence in 2026. The response plan targets 2.01 million of them.
Sexual assault made up 27% of reported protection incidents (August 2025), and 26% of women and girls avoid certain areas because they feel unsafe.
Two-thirds of women front-line responders saw a significant rise in sexual violence in 2025; half report further escalation in 2026.
One in five women working for women-led organisations has received threats.
8.1 million women of reproductive age and 805,000 pregnant women are in need of humanitarian assistance.
Maternal mortality was 256 deaths per 100,000 live births in 2023 and is believed to have risen since the war began.
37% of health facilities are not functioning.
27% of married women have an unmet need for family planning.
Almost 30% of households headed by women did not know where to find maternal and reproductive health services.
13.6 million women and girls need food and livelihoods support in 2026.
75% of households headed by women cannot meet basic food needs; only 1.9% are food secure, against 5.9% of households headed by men.
73% of women do not meet minimum dietary diversity, a risk for mothers and their babies.
Households headed by women are about 40% more likely to face extreme water deprivation.
4.1 million girls are out of school.
One in three women aged 20 to 24 was married before 18 (2014, latest survey).
One girl in seven is pregnant by the age of 18.
86.6% of women aged 15 to 49 have undergone female genital mutilation (2014, latest survey).
A Women's Advisory Group of 22 Sudanese and refugee women humanitarian leaders now informs senior humanitarian decisions.
99% of women-led organisations surveyed face funding shortages, obstruction or insecurity.
In the GBV coordination survey, all 58 organisations take part in coordination meetings, but more than half have no women with disabilities in their leadership.
